requirement: Metallic waste and scrap needs a pre-shipment inspection certificate from the country of origin, UNLESS it originates in a listed safe country (the USA is listed) AND enters through a designated seaport
source_ref: DGFT Public Notice 35/2026-27, 21 Oct 2026, amending HBP 2023 para 2.51(d)(v)(iv)
what_to_do: A US-origin container is exempt from PSIC only through a DESIGNATED seaport. Confirm Nhava Sheva is on the current designated list before the container sails.
how_to_verify: Get the text of DGFT Public Notice 35/2026-27 and read the designated-port list, or have the buyer's customs broker confirm in writing that the port of discharge is designated. Then: node scripts/export-rules.js verify IN-PSIC-2026 --by "<person>"
notes: DISPUTED ON PURPOSE, so this rule reports unknown rather than clear. Research on 2026-10-23 found secondary sources that disagree on the designated-port list: seasaw.ai described eight ports, steel-baba.com ten. Nobody produced the notice text itself. Nhava Sheva being on or off that list is the whole question.
Trans-shipment through a safe country is reported NOT to qualify — origin is what counts. Relevant if a container is ever routed via UAE, which is not on the safe list.
Maritime Gateway reports the exemption survives onward clearance at an inland container depot if the seaport checks are documented and the proof travels with the consignment.
SteelOrbis reported in September 2026 that the Indian government was considering relaxing the PSIC regime after recycler complaints. Expect this rule to move.

requirement: Metallic scrap entering India is subject to a radiation-screening regime at the port
source_ref: Referenced alongside the PSIC regime in trade commentary; primary source not obtained
what_to_do: Ask the buyer's broker what radiation documentation India expects from the exporter, and whether anything has to accompany the container.
how_to_verify: Buyer's customs broker at the port of discharge, in writing. Then: node scripts/export-rules.js verify IN-RADIATION --by "<person>"
notes: NEVER VERIFIED, so it reports unknown. Recorded rather than omitted because a rule nobody has written down is a rule nobody will ask about. The requirement line is deliberately vague — it says a regime exists, not what it demands, because that is the limit of what was established.

requirement: Unestablished — what South Korea requires of a US scrap exporter is not known
what_to_do: Do not treat a Busan container as clear on this file's say-so. Ask the buyer or Zimex what Korea asks for.
how_to_verify: Korea Customs Service (customs.go.kr), or a Korean customs broker, or the buyer. Then: node scripts/export-rules.js verify KR-SCRAP --by "<person>"
notes: Research on 2026-10-23 found NOTHING authoritative. A KOTRA customs guide lists the Nuclear Safety Act among applicable import laws without saying whether it reaches scrap shipments; trade.gov's guide is generic and does not mention scrap.

Radioactivity screening is common at scrap ports worldwide, so the absence of a source is not evidence there is no rule. That asymmetry is exactly why this row exists and why it is not marked allowed.
This is the most valuable row in the file. Busan is one of only two destinations in the codebase, and Jarvis does not know its rules.

requirement: China banned imports of most solid-waste scrap; a container of scrap is not expected to be admissible
source_ref: Widely reported policy effective 2021; primary instrument not obtained
what_to_do: Do not book scrap to a Chinese port without written confirmation from the buyer that the specific material is admissible under the current regime.
how_to_verify: Buyer's broker in China, in writing, naming the material. Then: node scripts/export-rules.js verify CN-SOLID-WASTE-BAN --by "<person>"
notes: Recorded from general industry knowledge, NOT from a source read on 2026-10-23, so it is unverified and reports unknown. Some categories were reclassified as resources rather than waste and are admissible, which is precisely the detail a blanket 'prohibited' would get wrong.
No Chinese port appears in the codebase today. This row is here so that the first time one is typed, Jarvis says 'ask' instead of nothing.
